articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft's latest Patch Tuesday fixes a whopping 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and Windows Defender's 'BlueHammer' flaw. When your security software has security flaws, you know we're living in the best timeline.

articles.title: Germany Doxes “UNKN,” Head of RU Ransomware Gangs REvil, GandCrab
articles.summary: Russian military intelligence exploited router vulnerabilities to mass-harvest Microsoft Office tokens, proving once again that your network is only as strong as your weakest IoT toaster. Classic APT move: why break down the front door when the back router is wide open?

articles.title: Open Records Laws Reveal ALPRs’ Sprawling Surveillance. Now States Want to Block What the Public Sees.
articles.summary: Utah's anti-VPN law goes live next week, because nothing says 'freedom' like legislating away privacy tools. Predictably, VPN usage surges wherever these ham-fisted age verification laws land—thanks for the marketing boost, lawmakers!

articles.title: Digital Hopes, Real Power: From Connection to Collective Action
articles.summary: FOIA requests exposed ALPR surveillance abuse, so naturally states want to block public oversight of license plate tracking dragnet. Can't have transparency ruining a perfectly good police state, can we?

articles.title: First reports come in of victims of critical cPanel vuln as 'millions' of sites potentially exposed
articles.summary: Senator Ron Wyden is catching heat from NSA bootlickers like Tom Cotton for demanding transparency about secret surveillance court opinions. When asking questions about government spying gets you threats, you know you're over the target.

articles.title: OpenAI locks GPT-5.5-Cyber behind velvet rope despite slamming Anthropic for doing exactly that
articles.summary: Critical cPanel vulnerability already being exploited in the wild, with ransomware gangs moving faster than patch deployment. CISA's known-exploited list grows while millions of hosting sites play vulnerability roulette.

articles.title: Poisoned Ruby Gems and Go Modules Exploit CI Pipelines for Credential Theft
articles.summary: Two cybersecurity professionals get 4 years for facilitating BlackCat ransomware attacks—when the defenders become the attackers, trust issues multiply exponentially. Nothing quite like insider knowledge weaponized for maximum chaos.

articles.title: Great responsibility, without great power
articles.summary: SonicWall firewall vulnerabilities allow security bypass and service crashes—your network's guardian becomes its weakest link. Emergency patches required before script kiddies turn your perimeter defense into Swiss cheese.

articles.title: Polymarket Rejects Data Breach Claims as Hacker Alleges 300K Records Stolen
articles.summary: French authorities probe 15-year-old who allegedly hacked the national ID agency and tried selling millions of citizen records on dark web. Kid's got skills but terrible OpSec—probably shouldn't have bragged about it online.

articles.title: Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431): Frequently asked questions about Linux kernel privilege escalation vulnerability
articles.summary: Sri Lanka loses over $3M in separate cyber incidents while recovering from debt crisis—hackers kicking a country when it's already down. Financial cybercrime hits different when your treasury is already running on fumes.
